  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.07</span>
    <span>Policy Optimization</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Is One Layer Enough? Training A Single Transformer Layer Can Match Full-Parameter RL Training</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces layer contribution to measure how much of full-parameter RL improvement can be recovered by training each transformer layer independently. Across multiple models, RL algorithms, and tasks, it finds that gains consistently concentrate in a few middle layers and that single-layer training can match or surpass full-parameter training.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01232" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>

</article>
<article class="paper-card" id="rethinking-the-divergence-regularization-in-llm-rl">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.06</span>
    <span>Policy Optimization</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Rethinking the Divergence Regularization in LLM RL</h3>
  <p>This paper proposes Divergence Regularized Policy Optimization (DRPO), replacing DPPO&#x27;s hard divergence mask with a smooth advantage-weighted quadratic regularizer that preserves its trust-region geometry. DRPO provides bounded continuous gradient weights and corrective signals beyond the trust-region boundary, improving LLM RL training stability and efficiency.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09821" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>

<article class="paper-card" id="constraint-infused-policy-optimization-principles-and-practices-for-harnessing-advanced-llm-reasoning">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.05</span>
    <span>Policy Optimization</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Constraint-Infused Policy Optimization: Principles and Practices for Harnessing Advanced LLM Reasoning</h3>
  <p>This paper formulates LLM reinforcement learning as constrained policy optimization, unifying existing algorithms through different constraint choices and exposing the roles of clipping, KL regularization, and trust regions. It derives Constraint-Infused Policy Optimization (CIPO), which improves reasoning performance and training stability across diverse tasks and model families.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16826" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>

  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2025.11</span>
    <span>Policy Optimization</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization (SAPO), replacing hard clipping in group-based LLM reinforcement learning with a temperature-controlled soft gate that continuously attenuates off-policy token updates. Its sequence-coherent, token-adaptive objective improves training stability, sample efficiency, and reasoning performance across text and Qwen3-VL models.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.20347" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>

    <span>Policy Optimization</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Group Sequence Policy Optimization</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces GSPO, a reinforcement learning algorithm for LLMs that replaces token-level importance ratios with sequence-level likelihood ratios and performs sequence-level clipping, rewarding, and optimization. GSPO improves training efficiency and performance over GRPO, stabilizes MoE RL training, and helps simplify large-scale RL infrastructure for Qwen3 models.</p>

  <h3>DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces Decoupled Clip and Dynamic Sampling Policy Optimization (DAPO), an open large-scale reinforcement learning system for eliciting LLM reasoning. It releases the training recipe, code, dataset, and model weights, reaching 50 points on AIME 2024 with Qwen2.5-32B and improving reproducibility for large-scale LLM RL.</p>

<article class="paper-card" id="provably-mitigating-overoptimization-in-rlhf-your-sft-loss-is-implicitly-an-adversarial-regularizer">
  <div class="paper-meta">

    <span>Policy Optimization</span>

  <h3>Provably Mitigating Overoptimization in RLHF: Your SFT Loss is Implicitly an Adversarial Regularizer</h3>
  <p>This paper identifies RLHF overoptimization as a consequence of distribution shift and uncertainty in learned preferences, then introduces Regularized Preference Optimization (RPO), which combines a preference optimization objective with an SFT loss that acts as an adversarial regularizer. RPO provides finite-sample guarantees and empirically improves alignment over DPO while reducing drift toward undesired responses.</p>

<article class="paper-card" id="kto-model-alignment-as-prospect-theoretic-optimization">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2024.02</span>
    <span>Policy Optimization</span>
  </div>
  <h3>KTO: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization</h3>
  <p>This paper frames successful LLM alignment losses as human-aware losses that encode biases from prospect theory, then introduces KTO to optimize generation utility directly from binary desirable/undesirable feedback. KTO matches or exceeds preference-pair methods from 1B to 30B scales, highlighting how the best alignment loss depends on the setting&#x27;s inductive biases.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01306" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>

</article>
<article class="paper-card" id="direct-preference-optimization-your-language-model-is-secretly-a-reward-model">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2023.05</span>
    <span>Policy Optimization</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), which reparameterizes the RLHF reward model so the optimal policy can be learned directly from preference data with a simple classification loss. DPO removes separate reward-model fitting and online reinforcement learning while matching or improving PPO-based RLHF with simpler, more stable training.</p>

  <h3>Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), a family of policy-gradient methods that alternates environment sampling with multiple minibatch epochs on a surrogate objective. PPO retains key trust-region benefits while being simpler to implement and empirically balancing sample efficiency, performance, and wall-clock time.</p>

  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.06</span>
    <span>OPD</span>
  </div>
  <h3>PowerOPD: Stabilizing On-Policy Distillation with Bounded Power Transformation</h3>
  <p>This paper identifies the unbounded log-ratio reward as the source of high-variance gradients and unstable training in sampled-token on-policy distillation. PowerOPD replaces it with a bounded, sign-consistent reward family derived from the Box-Cox power transformation, improving mathematical reasoning accuracy while reducing time and memory relative to full-vocabulary OPD.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17199" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>
  </div>
</article>
<article class="paper-card" id="anti-self-distillation-for-reasoning-rl-via-pointwise-mutual-information">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.05</span>
    <span>OPD</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Anti-Self-Distillation for Reasoning RL via Pointwise Mutual Information</h3>
  <p>This paper analyzes why on-policy self-distillation can hurt math reasoning, showing through pointwise mutual information that privileged context overemphasizes solution-implied tokens while suppressing deliberation tokens needed for search. It proposes AntiSD, which ascends rather than descends the self-distillation divergence with an entropy gate, reaching GRPO-level accuracy in 2 to 10x fewer steps and improving final accuracy by up to 11.5 points.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11609" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>

  </div>
</article>
<article class="paper-card" id="draft-opd-adapting-speculative-draft-models-from-llms-via-on-policy-distillation">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.05</span>
    <span>OPD</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Draft-OPD: Adapting Speculative Draft Models from LLMs via On-Policy Distillation</h3>
  <p>This paper proposes Draft-OPD, which adapts speculative draft models from RL-trained LLM traces through on-policy distillation without requiring expensive online generation for the draft model. It proves an equivalence between RL training and OPD-style distillation, reuses collected RL experience, and improves speculative decoding speed by up to 2.14x while preserving task performance.</p>

<article class="paper-card" id="omniopd-logit-free-on-policy-distillation-via-speculative-verification">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.05</span>
    <span>OPD</span>
  </div>
  <h3>OmniOPD: Logit-Free On-Policy Distillation via Speculative Verification</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces OmniOPD, a logit-free on-policy distillation framework that replaces brittle token-level logit matching with Monte Carlo chunk rollouts scored by semantic similarity, enabling black-box teachers. A peak-entropy scheduler focuses verification on uncertain reasoning forks, while Bayesian smoothing and a base-model KL anchor stabilize training; it outperforms standard OPD by up to 28.64% on math.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01476" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>

    <span>2026.04</span>
    <span>OPD</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Self-Distilled RLVR</h3>
  <p>This paper studies on-policy self-distillation for RLVR and shows that relying only on a privileged self-teacher can cause information leakage and unstable long-term training. It proposes RLSD, which uses self-distillation to estimate token-level update magnitudes while keeping RLVR&#x27;s environment feedback as the reliable update direction.</p>

    <span>OPD</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Learning beyond Teacher: Generalized On-Policy Distillation with Reward Extrapolation</h3>
  <p>This paper shows that on-policy distillation is a special case of dense KL-constrained RL, then proposes G-OPD with a flexible reference model and reward scaling factor. Its reward extrapolation variant, ExOPD, improves over standard OPD and can let students surpass domain teachers when merging RL-trained experts.</p>

<article class="paper-card" id="self-distilled-reasoner-on-policy-self-distillation-for-large-language-models">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.01</span>
    <span>OPD</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Self-Distilled Reasoner: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Language Models</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), where a single LLM acts as teacher and student under different contexts: the teacher sees privileged verified reasoning traces while the student samples from the question-only policy. By matching per-token distributions over the student&#x27;s on-policy rollouts, OPSD provides dense supervision without an external teacher and achieves stronger token efficiency than GRPO and off-policy distillation on math reasoning.</p>

  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.01</span>
    <span>OPD</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Self-Distillation Enables Continual Learning</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT), an on-policy self-distillation method that learns from expert demonstrations by using a demonstration-conditioned model as its own teacher. It improves new-task acquisition while reducing catastrophic forgetting, enabling sequential accumulation of skills and knowledge without explicit reward functions.</p>

  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.06</span>
    <span>Reward Modeling</span>
  </div>
  <h3>The Verification Horizon: No Silver Bullet for Coding Agent Rewards</h3>
  <p>This paper frames reliable verification as the emerging bottleneck for coding agents and evaluates reward signals by scalability, faithfulness, and robustness. Through test, rubric, user-feedback, and automated-agent verifiers, it shows that targeted designs can curb reward hacking and argues that verification must co-evolve with increasingly capable generators.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26300" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>

<article class="paper-card" id="bringing-value-models-back-generative-critics-for-value-modeling-in-llm-reinforcement-learning">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.04</span>
    <span>Reward Modeling</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Bringing Value Models Back: Generative Critics for Value Modeling in LLM Reinforcement Learning</h3>
  <p>This paper revisits value modeling for LLM reinforcement learning and argues that one-shot discriminative critics are limited by their expressiveness. It introduces Generative Actor-Critic (GenAC), whose critic reasons before estimating value and uses in-context conditioning to track the current actor, improving value approximation, ranking reliability, out-of-distribution generalization, and downstream RL performance.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10701" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>

    <span>Reward Modeling</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Reason Only When Needed: Efficient Generative Reward Modeling via Model-Internal Uncertainty</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces E-GRM, which estimates uncertainty from the convergence of parallel model generations and triggers chain-of-thought reasoning only when needed. A lightweight discriminative scorer trained with a hybrid regression-ranking objective provides fine-grained reasoning-path rewards, reducing inference cost while improving accuracy.</p>

  <h3>MemReward: Graph-Based Experience Memory for LLM Reward Prediction with Limited Labels</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces MemReward, a graph-based experience memory framework that achieves 97.3% of Oracle performance on 3B and 96.6% on 1.5B models for reward prediction with limited labels, surpassing Oracle in out-of-domain tasks.</p>

  <h3>Scaling Reward Modeling without Human Supervision</h3>
  <p>This paper studies unsupervised reward model scaling by learning preferences over web-corpus document prefixes and suffixes without human annotations. It reports consistent RewardBench gains across model backbones and shows downstream improvements in best-of-N selection and policy optimization.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">

  <h3>Reward Modeling from Natural Language Human Feedback</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces RLVR on preference data for training Generative Reward Models, demonstrating that binary classification tasks make GRMs susceptible to guessing correct outcomes without sound critiques, and proposes a method to address this limitation.</p>

    <span>Reward Modeling</span>
  </div>
  <h3>A Survey of Process Reward Models: From Outcome Signals to Process Supervisions for Large Language Models</h3>
  <p>This survey reviews Process Reward Models for evaluating and guiding LLM reasoning at the step or trajectory level rather than only judging final answers. It organizes the full loop of process data generation, PRM construction, and PRM use in test-time scaling and reinforcement learning across math, code, multimodal reasoning, robotics, and agents.</p>

  <p>This paper introduces VL-Calibration, a reinforcement learning framework that separates visual and reasoning confidence in large vision-language models to address confidently incorrect predictions.   <p>This paper presents FIPO, a reinforcement learning algorithm that overcomes reasoning bottlenecks in LLMs by addressing coarse-grained credit assignment in GRPO-style training, where outcome-based rewards fail to distinguish critical logical pivots from trivial tokens.</p>

  </div>
  <h3>The Entropy Mechanism of Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Language Models</h3>
  <p>This paper studies policy entropy collapse as a bottleneck in RL for reasoning language models, showing an empirical relationship between entropy and downstream performance that makes the performance ceiling predictable. It derives entropy dynamics from the covariance between action probability and logit updates, then proposes Clip-Cov and KL-Cov to preserve exploration and improve downstream performance.</p>

  <h3>OPID: On-Policy Skill Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</h3>
  <p>This paper proposes OPID, which extracts hierarchical episode- and step-level skills from completed on-policy trajectories and converts their effect into token-level self-distillation advantages alongside the outcome advantage. Its critical-first routing supplies dense, distribution-matched hindsight supervision, improving agent performance, sample efficiency, and robustness on embodied, web-shopping, and search-based tasks.</p>
